title: observability: token-level metrics + tracing dashboard improvements and alert tuning
author: Priya Patel
description: Motivation: improve token-level visibility for cost/latency breakdowns across our serving fleet and reduce noisy alerting during KV-cache warmups. This PR adds a revamped Grafana dashboard focusing on per-route and per-model token metrics, enhances tracing spans with token metadata, and tunes alert thresholds to reduce false positives while preserving SLO guardrails. Summary of changes: - New dashboards: token_cost_latency_overview, token_cache_hit_rate, route_token_breakdown. - Tracing: add token_count and token_cost annotations to serve_request spans; propagate model_variant and quantization_profile tags. - Metrics: emit token_generated_total, token_input_total, token_latency_bucket (histogram), token_cost_estimate gauge. - Alerts: adjust thresholds for token_latency_p95 and token_cost_rate for dedicated pools; add cooldown on alerts during autoscale events. Checklist: - [x] Metrics instrumented and unit-tested - [x] Dashboards added and validated on staging with synthetic workloads - [x] Alerts tuned and smoke-tested with alert-sim - [x] Docs updated: observability/README and alert runbook - [x] Backward compatible: metrics names added (no renames) Rollout plan: 1) Deploy metrics/tracing change to staging, run synthetic load to validate dashboards 2) Enable dashboards for platform and SRE teams 3) Deploy alerts with 72h monitoring window and ability to rollback 4) After 7 days, tighten thresholds if false positive rate below 1% Testing notes: used perf-canary to generate 1k req/s with varied sequence lengths and KV cache states; validated histogram buckets, tracing annotations, and alert cooldown behavior (alerts suppressed during scale-out). Related: ENG-8742 (token observability epic), ENG-8810 (alert tuning).
